headline: Severe sleep shortfall: rest today despite reassuring heart-rate recovery
summary: Last night's sleeping heart rate, resting heart rate, and HRV are reassuring, and yesterday's prescribed rest day was followed. However, Garmin recorded only 2h 28m sleep, a sleep score of 34, Body Battery 43 on waking, and Training Readiness 22. Six days after the marathon, the large sleep deficit is the decisive signal: do not run today.

recovery.label: Sleep
recovery.context: Poor; 5h 22m below Garmin's 7h 50m sleep need. Garmin recorded 1h 04m deep sleep and 48m REM.

recovery.label: Sleeping HR
recovery.context: 4.6 bpm below the prior 7-night average (63.6) and 5.7 bpm below the prior 14-night average (64.7). This is reassuring but cannot compensate for the very short sleep.

recovery.label: Resting HR
recovery.context: 6 bpm below Garmin's seven-day average of 59 and down from 62 yesterday.

recovery.label: HRV
recovery.context: Above Garmin's 42 ms weekly average; status remains balanced and its readiness contribution is very good.

recovery.label: Body Battery
recovery.context: Charged 31 points overnight and remained well below recent waking values of 66, 85, and 91.

recovery.label: Training Readiness
recovery.context: Garmin's strongest negative factor is sleep. Recovery time is about 6h 16m; acute load is 429 and the acute-to-chronic ratio is 0.8 (optimal).

recovery.label: Stress
recovery.context: An incomplete-day value captured around early afternoon; it is not directly comparable with a full day.

yesterday.title: Rest day completed
yesterday.summary: Garmin recorded no workout on 4 September. Daily activity was 4,851 steps, consistent with the prescribed recovery day.
yesterday.prescribed: No running; optional 20–30 minutes of easy walking or gentle flat cycling at RPE 1–2, with complete rest also appropriate.
yesterday.completed: No Garmin workout was recorded; daily activity totalled 4,851 steps.
yesterday.adherence_assessment: You followed the central instruction not to run or add training load. Complete rest was explicitly allowed, so the absence of a recorded optional walk or ride is compliant.
adherence_evidence: Zero Garmin activities were recorded on 4 September.
No running load or training effect was added.
The prior report explicitly allowed complete rest.
adherence_caveats: Garmin cannot verify unrecorded walking, mobility, perceived effort, pain, illness, or intent.
Daily steps show general movement but do not establish whether a structured recovery walk occurred.

environment.humidity_dew_point_context: Not applicable; no workout time to match against hourly weather.
environment.heat_impact_interpretation: Environmental strain did not affect workout adherence because no workout was recorded.
environment.limitations: General daily conditions cannot be assigned to a workout that did not occur.

recommendation.title: Full rest for the remainder of today
details: Do not run today. The 2h 28m sleep duration is the decisive recovery constraint despite favourable sleeping HR and HRV.
Optional only: 10–20 minutes of gentle indoor mobility or an easy walk after conditions cool, at RPE 1–2.
Prioritise food, fluids, a nap if naturally sleepy, and an early night. Reassess tomorrow from the next completed overnight record.
recommendation.alternative: Complete rest is preferred if you feel sleepy or depleted.
recommendation.reduce_or_stop: Stop optional activity if you feel unwell, unusually fatigued, dizzy, or if pain changes your movement. Symptoms and medical advice override Garmin scores.

signals.label: Sleep deficit
signals.interpretation: A 5h 22m shortfall substantially reduces recovery confidence and outweighs otherwise favourable autonomic markers.

signals.label: Autonomic recovery
signals.interpretation: These values are reassuring relative to recent baselines, but one favourable cluster does not make very short sleep adequate for training.

signals.label: Training load
signals.interpretation: Load is within Garmin's optimal range and yesterday added no workout, so today's rest is driven by sleep and post-marathon recovery rather than overload.

signals.label: Heat context
signals.interpretation: Very warm conditions and an extreme fire-weather warning make outdoor exercise a poor recovery trade-off this afternoon.

caveats: Garmin's sleep-stage estimates are wearable-derived, but the total duration is sufficiently low to drive a conservative decision.
Today's stress and Body Battery values are incomplete and reflect the day only through the latest sync.
No humidity or dew-point measurement was needed for yesterday because there was no recorded workout.
Current Sydney weather is city-level context, not route-level measurement.
